disposition: ACCEPT — scoped original course content and guide
scope: Read all 12 questions, explanations/transfers and complete guide; final read verifies the precise question5/general exchange-proof corrections. No helper, UI, generated page, browser or automated-test acceptance.

findings.original: Question5 and the general cut-property proof promised a global spanning tree without requiring a connected input.
findings.counterexample: A component containing A and B has crossing edges of weights2,5,7 while another vertex is isolated. A minimum spanning forest exists; a global spanning tree does not.
findings.resolution: Final text consistently states a compatible minimum spanning forest and confines the exchange to the original connected component.

findings.original: The first corrected exchange explanation omitted the already-included-edge case.
findings.resolution: Final text explicitly needs no exchange when the chosen edge already belongs to a compatible minimum forest; otherwise addition creates a within-component cycle and removal of a crossing edge of no smaller weight preserves minimum weight.

hand_checks: Connected worked example accepts weights1,2,3: total6 with5 edge decisions.
Tied triangle accepts two weight1 edges: total2; deterministic input order does not imply uniqueness.
Disconnected example -2+1+2=1; isolated vertices remain components and accepted count is n-k.
Spanning-tree route2+2=4 need not equal original direct shortest route3.
Complete edge-decision counts are explicitly distinguished from sorting/component-operation counts.
limits: No numerical test rerun after wording-only correction.
Root separately receives algorithm helper; local and remote separately receive UI/browser.
